potentials.title: EAM potential for Cu by Zhou, Johnson and Wadley (2004), NIST retabulation v001
potentials.content_origin: NIST Interatomic Potentials Repository, retabulated by L. M. Hale (NIST) from Zhou04_create_v2.f to remove single/double precision fluctuations in the original tables
potentials.license_text: This work is dedicated to the public domain.

citations: X. W. Zhou, R. A. Johnson and H. N. G. Wadley, Misfit-energy-increasing dislocations in vapor-deposited CoFe/NiFe multilayers, Phys. Rev. B 69 (2004) 144113, doi:10.1103/PhysRevB.69.144113
X. W. Zhou, H. N. G. Wadley, R. A. Johnson et al., Atomic scale structure of sputtered metal multilayers, Acta Mater. 49 (2001) 4005, doi:10.1016/S1359-6454(01)00287-7
M. S. Daw and M. I. Baskes, Embedded-atom method, Phys. Rev. B 29 (1984) 6443, doi:10.1103/PhysRevB.29.6443
OpenKIM archive of this model, doi:10.25950/a2be92ad
potentials.interpolation: cubic Hermite with fourth-order finite-difference slopes, as in LAMMPS pair_style eam/alloy and the OpenKIM EAM_Dynamo driver (MD_120291908751_006, doi:10.25950/233cb735)
notes: Fitted as a member of a sixteen-element database intended for vapor-deposited metal multilayers. Its authors state it was not designed for intermetallic compounds.

The lattice-type field in the file header reads fcc for every element of the database, including W. The setfl format does not use that field and neither does Materia; the equilibrium structure is established by calculation.
Each file contains one element. Materia does not combine files, so no alloy is offered from these potentials.
